description: Canonical database benchmark cases. Every language client reads this file, so SQL text, iteration counts, setup and per-case verification are identical across clients by construction. Parameter generators are named here and implemented with the same formula in every client (see README.md).

cases.note: One prepared INSERT per row, one implicit transaction per row.
cases.sql: INSERT INTO bench_writes (id, k, payload, tag) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)

checks.sql: SELECT count(*)::bigint, count(DISTINCT id)::bigint FROM bench_writes

cases.note: One prepared INSERT per row, all rows in a single transaction.

cases.note: Aggregation over the whole read dataset.
cases.sql: SELECT tag, count(*)::bigint AS n, sum(k)::bigint AS total FROM bench_events GROUP BY tag ORDER BY tag

cases.note: Two-table JOIN, 100 rows per query.
cases.sql: SELECT o.id, o.qty, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.id LIMIT 100

cases.note: Three-table JOIN starting at a deterministic order id.
cases.sql: SELECT o.id, o.qty, c.name, p.sku FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.id >= $1 ORDER BY o.id LIMIT 100

cases.note: INNER JOIN aggregation filtered by order status.
cases.sql: SELECT count(*)::bigint FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = $1

cases.note: LEFT JOIN: every customer in the first 100, including those with no order.
cases.sql: SELECT c.id, count(o.id)::bigint FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.id <= 100 GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY c.id

cases.note: Aggregation with JOIN grouped by customer city.
cases.sql: SELECT c.city, sum(o.qty)::bigint AS units, count(*)::bigint AS orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY c.city

cases.note: Create a product.
cases.sql: INSERT INTO products (id, sku, name, category, price, stock) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::text::numeric, $6)

cases.note: Retrieve product details by id.
cases.sql: SELECT id, sku, name, category, price::text AS price, stock FROM products WHERE id = $1

cases.note: Search products by category with a name prefix.
cases.sql: SELECT id, sku, name FROM products WHERE category = $1 AND name LIKE $2 ORDER BY id LIMIT 20

cases.note: Reduce stock quantity with a stock >= qty guard.
cases.sql: UPDATE products SET stock = stock - $2 WHERE id = $1 AND stock >= $2

checks.sql: SELECT count(*)::bigint FROM products WHERE stock < 0

cases.note: Create a customer.
cases.sql: INSERT INTO customers (id, email, name, city) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)

cases.note: Create an order against existing products and customers.
cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, product_id, qty, unit_price, status) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::text::numeric, $6)

cases.note: Create an order and reduce inventory in one transaction; roll back when stock is insufficient.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*)::bigint FROM products WHERE stock < 0
SELECT count(*)::bigint FROM orders o LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE p.id IS NULL
SELECT count(*)::bigint FROM orders WHERE id >= 2000000

cases.note: Retrieve order details with a three-table JOIN.
cases.sql: SELECT o.id, o.qty, p.sku, c.name FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id = $1

cases.note: Calculate sales totals for a status.
cases.sql: SELECT (sum(qty * unit_price))::numeric(14, 2)::text AS total FROM orders WHERE status = $1

cases.note: Generate an inventory report grouped by category.
cases.sql: SELECT category, count(*)::bigint AS items, sum(stock)::bigint AS units, (sum(stock * price))::numeric(14, 2)::text AS value FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
